use_cases.title: Private AI
use_cases.description: Private AI workloads, local model serving, and user-facing AI workbench intent.

use_cases.title: ai-assistant
use_cases.description: Hermes Agent personal assistant with persistent memory and skills on the node's local model, selected with the Private AI assistant module. It inspects and drafts by default; messaging, web search, schedules and external writes are toolsets the owner grants in Hermes. Its dashboard is reached only on a private route behind the kit's login and its own password.

use_cases.title: ai-control-plane
use_cases.description: Paperclip agent control plane (org chart of agents, budgets, approvals, tasks) with its own PostgreSQL in one gVisor-isolated bundle, selected with the Private AI agent-control-plane module. Budgets default to zero and no provider key is configured; the installed Hermes is reachable on the private AI network. Reached only on a private route behind the kit's login and Paperclip's own login.

use_cases.title: ai-documents
use_cases.description: Document text extraction for Open WebUI through Apache Tika, or Docling for scanned and complex layouts, selected with the Private AI document-parsing module. It joins the node's private AI network and has no route of its own.

use_cases.title: ai-gateway
use_cases.description: LiteLLM model router that gives the owner's apps and devices one OpenAI-compatible endpoint for the node's Ollama models, selected with the Private AI model-router module. Every request needs the master key from owner custody; the route is local or remote-private, never public.

use_cases.title: ai-harness
use_cases.description: OpenHands task and coding agent whose shell, editor and automations run inside one gVisor-isolated container with its own workspace volume and the node's Ollama as model endpoint, selected with the Private AI agent-harness module. Reached only on a private route behind the kit's login.

use_cases.title: ai-image-video
use_cases.description: ComfyUI image and video generation on the node's CPU or selected GPU with reviewed workflow templates, selected with the Private AI image-video module. ComfyUI has no sign-in of its own, so it is reached only on a private route behind the kit's login.

use_cases.title: ai-search
use_cases.description: Private SearXNG meta search that Open WebUI uses for web search, selected with the Private AI web-search module. It joins the node's private AI network and has no route of its own.

use_cases.title: ai-speech
use_cases.description: kombify SpeechKit server with local speech providers (Parakeet STT, Kokoro TTS, the node's Ollama for Assist), selected with the Private AI speech module. It serves the chat module on the node's private AI network and the household's devices on the LAN (port 18080, announced over mDNS as _speechkit._tcp), each behind its bearer or device token.

use_cases.title: ai-vectors
use_cases.description: Qdrant vector store that holds the chat module's knowledge-base vectors (embeddings from bge-m3 on the node's Ollama), selected with the Private AI vector-store module. It joins the node's private AI network, needs the API key from owner custody on every request and is local or remote-private, never public.

use_cases.title: automation-notifications
use_cases.description: Explicit ntfy live-only notification add-on: forward to connected subscribers; no queued replay, native accounts, Web Push or attachments. Durable push and backup digest delivery remain separate prerequisites.

use_cases.title: basement-core
use_cases.description: Required standalone Basement control plane with local routing, owner identity, internal PKI, container management, and operator hub.

use_cases.title: Private AI
use_cases.description: Private AI workloads, local model serving, and user-facing AI workbench intent.

use_cases.title: ai-assistant
use_cases.description: Hermes Agent personal assistant with persistent memory and skills on the node's local model, selected with the Private AI assistant module. It inspects and drafts by default; messaging, web search, schedules and external writes are toolsets the owner grants in Hermes. Its dashboard is reached only on a private route behind the kit's login and its own password.

use_cases.title: ai-control-plane
use_cases.description: Paperclip agent control plane (org chart of agents, budgets, approvals, tasks) with its own PostgreSQL in one gVisor-isolated bundle, selected with the Private AI agent-control-plane module. Budgets default to zero and no provider key is configured; the installed Hermes is reachable on the private AI network. Reached only on a private route behind the kit's login and Paperclip's own login.

use_cases.title: ai-documents
use_cases.description: Document text extraction for Open WebUI through Apache Tika, or Docling for scanned and complex layouts, selected with the Private AI document-parsing module. It joins the node's private AI network and has no route of its own.

use_cases.title: ai-gateway
use_cases.description: LiteLLM model router that gives the owner's apps and devices one OpenAI-compatible endpoint for the node's Ollama models, selected with the Private AI model-router module. Every request needs the master key from owner custody; the route is local or remote-private, never public.

use_cases.title: ai-harness
use_cases.description: OpenHands task and coding agent whose shell, editor and automations run inside one gVisor-isolated container with its own workspace volume and the node's Ollama as model endpoint, selected with the Private AI agent-harness module. Reached only on a private route behind the kit's login.

use_cases.title: ai-image-video
use_cases.description: ComfyUI image and video generation on the node's CPU or selected GPU with reviewed workflow templates, selected with the Private AI image-video module. ComfyUI has no sign-in of its own, so it is reached only on a private route behind the kit's login.

use_cases.title: ai-search
use_cases.description: Private SearXNG meta search that Open WebUI uses for web search, selected with the Private AI web-search module. It joins the node's private AI network and has no route of its own.

use_cases.title: ai-speech
use_cases.description: kombify SpeechKit server with local speech providers (Parakeet STT, Kokoro TTS, the node's Ollama for Assist), selected with the Private AI speech module. It serves the chat module on the node's private AI network and the household's devices on the LAN (port 18080, announced over mDNS as _speechkit._tcp), each behind its bearer or device token.

use_cases.title: ai-vectors
use_cases.description: Qdrant vector store that holds the chat module's knowledge-base vectors (embeddings from bge-m3 on the node's Ollama), selected with the Private AI vector-store module. It joins the node's private AI network, needs the API key from owner custody on every request and is local or remote-private, never public.

use_cases.title: automation-notifications
use_cases.description: Explicit ntfy live-only notification add-on: forward to connected subscribers; no queued replay, native accounts, Web Push or attachments. Durable push and backup digest delivery remain separate prerequisites.

use_cases.title: cloud-core
use_cases.description: Required provider-neutral Cloud control plane installed on an externally supplied host; provider and server lifecycle remain outside StackKits.

use_cases.title: Developer Platform
use_cases.description: Private source control, developer collaboration, and delivery-platform intent.

use_cases.title: dev-workbench
use_cases.description: Optional pinned Workbench Cloud Linux host; Connect enrollment and provider configuration are explicit owner setup. Resource floors are policy, runtime acceptance is pending M13.

use_cases.title: Documents
use_cases.description: Private document ingestion, OCR, indexing and search through Paperless-ngx.

use_cases.title: File Storage and Documents
use_cases.description: Private file storage and sharing: Cloudreve by default, Nextcloud or kombify Paperwork as alternatives, with optional office editing and a document archive.

use_cases.title: files-office
use_cases.description: Euro-Office Document Server for browser editing of documents, spreadsheets and presentations, selected in addition to the files workload and connected to Nextcloud through the eurooffice-nextcloud app.

use_cases.title: Game Server
use_cases.description: Self-hosted game servers for friends and family through Calagopus (or Pelican or Pterodactyl), with curated Minecraft Java, Paper and Bedrock, Terraria and Valheim profiles.

use_cases.title: Private Mail
use_cases.description: Private webmail through Roundcube for a mailbox you already have at an external provider. No mail server, DNS or MX record is created.

use_cases.title: Own Mail Server
use_cases.description: Your own mail server on a dedicated Cloud node through Stalwart: mailboxes for your domain with SMTP, IMAP and submission. StackKits prints the DNS records you publish; it never changes DNS.

use_cases.title: Marketplace
use_cases.description: Your own app store for applications you run on your homelab, at home and in the cloud.

use_cases.title: Media Library
use_cases.description: Private media library and streaming intent for household media collections.

use_cases.title: media-music

use_cases.title: Photos and Memories

use_cases.title: Private AI
use_cases.description: Private AI workloads, local model serving, and user-facing AI workbench intent.

use_cases.title: ai-assistant
use_cases.description: Hermes Agent personal assistant with persistent memory and skills on the node's local model, selected with the Private AI assistant module. It inspects and drafts by default; messaging, web search, schedules and external writes are toolsets the owner grants in Hermes. Its dashboard is reached only on a private route behind the kit's login and its own password.

use_cases.title: ai-control-plane
use_cases.description: Paperclip agent control plane (org chart of agents, budgets, approvals, tasks) with its own PostgreSQL in one gVisor-isolated bundle, selected with the Private AI agent-control-plane module. Budgets default to zero and no provider key is configured; the installed Hermes is reachable on the private AI network. Reached only on a private route behind the kit's login and Paperclip's own login.

use_cases.title: ai-documents
use_cases.description: Document text extraction for Open WebUI through Apache Tika, or Docling for scanned and complex layouts, selected with the Private AI document-parsing module. It joins the node's private AI network and has no route of its own.

use_cases.title: ai-gateway
use_cases.description: LiteLLM model router that gives the owner's apps and devices one OpenAI-compatible endpoint for the node's Ollama models, selected with the Private AI model-router module. Every request needs the master key from owner custody; the route is local or remote-private, never public.

use_cases.title: ai-harness
use_cases.description: OpenHands task and coding agent whose shell, editor and automations run inside one gVisor-isolated container with its own workspace volume and the node's Ollama as model endpoint, selected with the Private AI agent-harness module. Reached only on a private route behind the kit's login.

use_cases.title: ai-image-video

use_cases.title: ai-search

use_cases.title: ai-speech
use_cases.description: kombify SpeechKit server with local speech providers (Parakeet STT, Kokoro TTS, the node's Ollama for Assist), selected with the Private AI speech module. operations.title: List add-ons
operations.description: Use before installing or changing an add-on. Lists the add-ons this StackKit offers; reads only.

operations.title: Bind public addresses
operations.description: Use after an address is allocated to apply it. Writes the bound public routes into a new validated spec file; existing intent is replaced only when its exact current hash is passed.

operations.title: Plan public addresses
operations.description: Use before binding a public address, to see what registration needs. Prints the account-free address plan; changes nothing.

operations.title: Apply Advanced change set
operations.description: Use after the change set is created and reviewed. Applies it and verifies the result, rolling back automatically on failure; the running stack changes.

operations.title: Create Advanced change set
operations.description: Use before an Advanced apply to turn a candidate spec into something reviewable. Writes a content-addressed, Owner-signed change set; applies nothing.

operations.title: Run restore drill
operations.description: Use to prove a backup restores without risking the live homelab. Creates or reuses an anchor, stages and verifies a restore, then removes the staging copy; the live runtime is left as it was.

operations.title: Run coordinated rollback
operations.description: Use when an Advanced apply must be undone. Rolls every local stack back to one verified checkpoint, newest first; stacks added after the checkpoint are destroyed.

operations.title: Import Advanced trust
operations.description: Use to trust one known Advanced issuer. Imports the exact pinned bundle into local owner trust and replaces the record that was there.

operations.title: Inspect Advanced trust
operations.description: Use before any Advanced operation to see which issuer this host trusts. Reads the verified local trust; changes nothing.

operations.title: Application compatibility
operations.description: Use before choosing an application or a delivery adapter. Shows the fixed support matrix; it reports product capability, not what this plan or host runs.

operations.title: Operate an own application
operations.description: Use to run one extra container image, or one Compose project of several containers, beside the homelab. Dry-run the exact action to review Compose, routing and backup, then repeat it with the returned digest; remove keeps data unless deletion is explicit.

operations.title: Adopt application
operations.description: Use after stackkit_application_inspect to put an existing application under lifecycle custody. Signs the reviewed binding and keeps its accounts, configuration and data.

operations.title: Control adopted application
operations.description: Use to start, stop or restart an adopted application without changing it. Acts on the exact adopted container; nothing is recreated and no configuration changes.

operations.title: Assess application adoption
operations.description: Use before adopting an application that already runs on this host. Reads the container, its current configuration and what must be preserved; changes nothing.

operations.title: Release adopted application
operations.description: Use to hand an adopted application back to manual management. Releases lifecycle custody and keeps the application and its data running.

operations.title: Verify adopted application
operations.description: Use after adoption, or when custody looks wrong. Checks the signed binding against the current source; reads only.

operations.title: Apply
operations.description: Use when the plan is reviewed and the user wants it live. Applies the exact saved plan to this host, which starts the services it declares.

operations.title: Backup
operations.description: Use when the user wants a snapshot now, outside the schedule. Creates one local backup snapshot in owner custody; the running services keep running.

operations.title: Configure backup repository
operations.description: Use once per host, or after the backup policy changes. Configures the local repository from the generated policy, whose path and service cannot be overridden.

operations.title: Emergency export
operations.description: Use before a move or a disaster, when snapshots are not enough. Writes a new age-encrypted portable archive with checksums and a runbook; it copies files, so stop writers for a consistent export.

operations.title: Emergency restore
operations.description: Use to inspect or stage a portable archive on another host. Decrypts and verifies it into a new staging directory; nothing is activated.

operations.title: Activate restore
operations.description: Use after a restore is staged and reviewed. Copies the staged data into the live volumes, taking an automatic safety snapshot first.

operations.title: Recover restore
operations.description: Use when a restore activation was interrupted. Rolls back before the commit or finishes the committed result; repeating it returns the original result.

operations.title: Disable backup schedule
operations.description: Use to stop scheduled backups. Stops the backup timer and revokes its authorization; existing snapshots are kept.

operations.title: Enable backup schedule
operations.description: Use to turn scheduled backups on. Enables the backup timer at the cadence the spec declares; the next run happens on that timer.

operations.title: Backup schedule status
operations.description: Use to check whether scheduled backups run and when the last one happened. Reads the timer, its authorization and the last snapshot separately; changes nothing.

operations.title: Backup status
operations.description: Use before a restore, or when a backup looks missing. Reads repository readiness, snapshot history and the declared recovery objectives; changes nothing.

operations.title: Backup target status
operations.description: Use when a backup target looks unreachable, or to check its custody. Verifies local target custody and returns opaque references only; no remote storage is contacted.

operations.title: List break-glass bundles
operations.description: Use during an outage to find the offline recovery bundles. Lists the encrypted break-glass bundles on this host; reads only.

operations.title: Show break-glass bundle
operations.description: Use after stackkit_break_glass_list to get the exact file. Prints the path of one node's still-encrypted bundle; decrypts nothing.

operations.title: Configure capability
operations.description: Use to enable or change one declared Foundation capability. Merges public settings, a provider and custody references into the spec by hash; no service changes until apply.

operations.title: Capacity
operations.description: Use before choosing or resizing modules, or when this host may be too small. Compares the selected modules with observed host capacity; missing measurements stay unverified and nothing is reserved.

operations.title: Compatibility diagnostics
operations.description: Use before installing on an unusual host or operating system. Shows the published support evidence and runs non-destructive host diagnostics; it certifies no server.

operations.title: Drift
operations.description: Use to see whether the host still matches the plan. Compares desired, applied and live state; fixes nothing, so use stackkit_drift_reconcile to fix it.

operations.title: Reconcile drift
operations.description: Use when stackkit_drift reports a difference. Checkpoints, then generates, applies and verifies, rolling back on failure; the running stack changes.

operations.title: Feasibility
operations.description: Use before apply when the spec pins workloads to nodes. Reports per-workload and per-node fit against an exact inventory; records nothing and runs nothing.

operations.title: Adopt Federation binding
operations.description: Use to bring an external host into this homelab's inventory. Validates, Owner-signs and adopts the binding in one step.

operations.title: Import Federation binding
operations.description: Use to record a binding that is already Owner-signed. Admits it into local inventory; no remote system changes.

operations.title: Bind Federation control receiver
operations.description: Use to point this receiver at a Home. Admits the Home's public authority and the local receiver custody, replacing the previous receiver authority.

operations.title: Send Federation control action
operations.description: Use to deliver a signed action to a Cloud node. Sends it over the exact pinned Home-initiated connection, so the remote node is reached.

operations.title: Sign Federation control action
operations.description: Use to sign one plan or verify action for a Cloud node. Signs with the current Home custody and returns the action; nothing is sent.

operations.title: Withdraw Federation control receiver
operations.description: Use to cut a receiver off for good. Withdraws receiver authority and ends its TLS sessions; the withdrawal stands on later runs.

operations.title: Bind Federation link
operations.description: Use to adopt an existing WireGuard fabric link. Adopts the handles into local owner custody; the remote fabric is not changed.

operations.title: Stop Federation link
operations.description: Use to take an adopted link down temporarily. Stops the interface and keeps the external fabric, so nothing is deleted.

operations.title: Admit game player
operations.description: Use to let one player onto an allow-list game server. Adds the account and reads the allow list back; only that server's list changes.

operations.title: List game servers
operations.description: Use first for game servers: it names the identifiers the other game tools take. Lists the owner's game servers with state and port; reads only.

operations.title: Game server power
operations.description: Use with an identifier from stackkit_game_list. Starts, stops or restarts one game server and waits until the new state is observed.

operations.title: Generate
operations.description: Use after stackkit_resolve to render what apply would deploy. Writes the rollout artifacts for the exact saved plan; deploys nothing.

operations.title: Attach host conformance
operations.description: Use before planning for a host that is not this machine. Attaches the host binding and its conformance receipt to the inventory; changes only that inventory file.

operations.title: Host conformance receipt
operations.description: Use to measure a host against the binding used for planning. Produces a provider-neutral conformance receipt on stdout or in a workspace file; installs nothing.

operations.title: Host environment
operations.description: Use before init to know which addresses fit. Detects whether this host looks like a home network or a public server; observes only.

operations.title: Host preflight
operations.description: Use before apply to check whether this host can run the selected StackKit. Measures against the kit's floor and changes nothing; apply repeats the same check.

operations.title: Prepare Cloud host
operations.description: Use to converge a Cloud Kit host after an interrupted install; installers and apply run it themselves. Provisions the execution-channel Linux account, its privileges and the workspace-held SSH key.

operations.title: Reboot host
operations.description: Use after updates when the node must restart. Schedules a guarded reboot that waits for running package work; a control-plane node or one that cannot boot unattended is refused.

operations.title: Remediate host
operations.description: Use when preflight names a finding that has a fix. Plans the reversible fixes, or carries out one named fix; without apply nothing changes.

operations.title: Apply host updates
operations.description: Use with the digest from stackkit_host_updates_plan. Installs exactly that reviewed package set on this node and reports version changes; a stale plan is refused.

operations.title: Plan host updates
operations.description: Use before updating packages, to see what would change. Refreshes the package index and lists pending updates with a digest; installs nothing.

operations.title: Apply identity projection
operations.description: Use after the projection is approved to make it live. Applies that exact projection to local PocketID; local accounts and groups change.

operations.title: Approve identity projection
operations.description: Use after stackkit_identity_projection_inspect. Creates the Owner-signed approval and leaves PocketID untouched; stackkit_identity_projection_apply makes it live.

operations.title: Inspect identity projection
operations.description: Use before approving an identity projection. Verifies the signed, credential-free document; changes nothing.

operations.title: Unlink identity projection
operations.description: Use to detach optional identity sync. Detaches the linked projection without deleting any local identity.

operations.title: Enroll workload peer
operations.description: Use with that request to issue a credential. Issues and admits one workload peer for an installed Home publication; returns only public certificates.

operations.title: Install workload peer
operations.description: Use to install the issued certificate on the workload host. Writes that peer's credential under a Home root verified through a separate channel.

operations.title: Probe workload peer
operations.description: Use to check that a workload answers through the tunnel. Requests the origin through an existing loopback socket; reads only.

operations.title: Request workload peer
operations.description: Use first on a workload host that needs a Home certificate. Creates or reuses the local key and returns only the public request; no admission changes.

operations.title: Revoke workload peer
operations.description: Use when a workload certificate should stop working. Withdraws the peer's current Home admission; the old certificate is no longer accepted.

operations.title: Init
operations.description: Use when the user wants a new homelab or has no stack-spec.yaml yet. Writes the spec from the chosen kit's defaults and asks for the email address of the person who becomes the first owner; installs nothing.

operations.title: List releases
operations.description: Use to find which StackKits releases exist. Fetches the public release index; reads only.

operations.title: Logs
operations.description: Use to find a past run. Lists the local structured rollout logs; then read one with stackkit_logs_read.

operations.title: Read logs
operations.description: Use after stackkit_logs to read one run. Returns one page of structured events, newest by default; changes nothing.

operations.title: Migrate StackSpec v1
operations.description: Use to move an older stack-spec.yaml forward. Classifies it and reports what must be done by hand; a new file is written only when asked, and nothing is upgraded in place.

operations.title: Lint modules
operations.description: Use before submitting a module change. Lints module CUE for pin, health, security and access hygiene; changes nothing.

operations.title: Scaffold module
operations.description: Use to start a new module from its facts file. Renders the module artifacts or prints them; existing files are overwritten only with force.

operations.title: Collect retired output transaction
operations.description: Use to clean up after a retired output transaction. Inspects the tombstone by default and removes it only when apply is set.

operations.title: Plan
operations.description: Use to review what apply would do. Reads the saved plan and the generated artifacts; changes nothing.

operations.title: Prepare check
operations.description: Use before init or apply to see whether this machine is ready. Runs the read-only host checks that apply also runs; installs nothing.

operations.title: Registry info
operations.description: Use to inspect the catalog copy bundled with this binary. Summarizes the embedded registry snapshot; reads only.

operations.title: Remove
operations.description: Use to uninstall a workload, or the whole homelab when no workload is named. Stops and removes the selected workloads; data volumes stay unless data deletion is explicit.

operations.title: Resolve
operations.description: Use after editing the spec and before stackkit_generate. Computes the canonical plan from the spec and observed inventory; nothing is applied.

operations.title: Restore
operations.description: Use to restore one signed snapshot. Verifies it and restores into isolated staging; live volumes change only with stackkit_backup_restore_activate.

operations.title: Abandon restore
operations.description: Use to close a restore that will not continue. Ends one pending or staged restore journal; the repository and live volumes are left alone.

operations.title: Materialize secret custody
operations.description: Use after adding a workload and before stackkit_generate. Establishes local custody for every declared secret; values are never returned.

operations.title: Service logs
operations.description: Use to read what one service logged. Returns bounded, redacted entries for one managed service; changes nothing.

operations.title: Restart service
operations.description: Use to restart one managed service without touching its data. Restarts only that service; the rest of the stack keeps running.

operations.title: Start service
operations.description: Use to bring back a service that was stopped. Starts one service declared by the active plan; only that service changes.

operations.title: Stop service
operations.description: Use to take one non-critical service offline. Stops only that service; core services such as base, id and auth are refused.

operations.title: Set up application
operations.description: Use after apply when an application declares a setup action such as its owner account. Runs that one action against the live application; credentials stay out of the evidence.

operations.title: Status
operations.description: Use to see where the homelab stands and what runs now. Reads deployment state, services, health and URLs; changes nothing.

operations.title: Export support evidence
operations.description: Use to hand one run to support. Writes that rollout log and its receipts to a new local file; no runtime changes.

operations.title: Upgrade
operations.description: Use to move this homelab to another StackKits release. Verifies the release, checkpoints for rollback, then installs and applies it; the running stack changes.

operations.title: Add use case
operations.description: Use to add one application from the kit catalog. Writes it into the spec and prepares its local secret slots; nothing is deployed until apply.

operations.title: Configure use case
operations.description: Use to change the settings or profiles of one chosen application. Merges them into the spec and keeps everything omitted; no service changes until apply.

operations.title: Change application release
operations.description: Use to move one application to a newer release of its entry image, tested or owner-accepted untested inside its release track. Stops it and checkpoints its data for rollback; apply (or --apply in one step, with automatic rollback) starts the new release and finalize drops the checkpoint.

operations.title: Application release overrides
operations.description: Use to see which applications run their own release override and whether the installed StackKits release keeps or supersedes it; changes nothing.

operations.title: Application release status
operations.description: Use to see where an application release change stands. Reads the Owner-signed record, the retained volumes and their read-back; changes nothing.

operations.title: List users
operations.description: Use before adding or removing a household member. Lists household users in local PocketID; reads only.

operations.title: Owner activation status
operations.description: Use when the owner cannot sign in. Reads the owner passkey activation status without its activation link; changes nothing.

operations.title: Remove user
operations.description: Use to remove a household member for good. Revokes their devices and sessions and deletes the PocketID user; the owner and admins are refused.

operations.title: Validate
operations.description: Use to check the spec and kit definitions before planning. Reads and validates only; changes no lifecycle state.

operations.title: Verify
operations.description: Use after stackkit_apply, or when something looks wrong. Runs read-only checks across desired, planned, applied and observed state.
